subject: Post-incident postmortem and remediation plan for inference-rate degradation
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fluxdata.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@fluxdata.com>, FluxData SRE <sre@fluxdata.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Observed throughput drop — Redwood inference service (us-west-2)

Hi Jasmine,

We noticed a sustained drop in inference throughput starting ~12:45 PST today for our us-west-2 endpoint. Requests are queuing; effective tokens/sec are down ~35–45% for our steady-state workload. This hit our ingestion pipeline during a high-traffic batch and caused retries in a downstream job.

Quick details:
- Endpoint: rwd-api.prod.us-west-2.fluxdata
- Impact window: ~12:45–13:10 PST (we still see elevated latency)
- Error class: mostly 504s and longer tail latencies; some requests were retried by the client and succeeded later.

Can you confirm you're seeing the same on Redwood's side and share an ETA for mitigation? We can provide additional traces if that helps. This is priority for us — happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Nguyen
SRE, FluxData Labs
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fluxdata.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@fluxdata.com>, FluxData SRE <sre@fluxdata.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed throughput drop — Redwood inference service (us-west-2)

Hi Alex — thanks for the flag and the initial details. We're seeing increased p99/p999 latency on the same cluster and a corresponding drop in throughput on our monitoring.

Immediate actions (already in motion):
- Jonas and Hannah are collecting server-side traces and KV/cache heatmaps — I'll make sure you get the logs we can share.
- We've temporarily enabled an emergency routing policy to shift some traffic to warm replicas to reduce cold-starts.
- We will provide a short RCA and proposed remediation timeline by EOD tomorrow.

Are you able to share a short sample trace (request id) for one of the failed requests? That will help confirm correlation.

I'll follow up with a concise postmortem and next steps. If you prefer a call, I'm available 14:00–15:00 PST.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: internal: quick triage notes for FluxData throughput drop

Team — quick log dump and earliest hypothesis. (Forwarding Alex's original message below.)

Findings so far:
- At ~12:44 PST we saw an abrupt spike in unique conversation prefixes which caused KV cache churn. The cache eviction rate increased ~6x.
- Autoscaler activity: a delayed scale-up event coincided with the churn; new instances were added but entered ready state slowly due to a kernel-level page fault pattern that increased cold-start time.
- The combination reduced batching efficiency; effective batch size dropped ~40%, which lowered tokens/sec despite overall capacity being nominal.

Immediate mitigations applied at 13:00 PST:
- Activated emergency routing to warm nodes (Jasmine executed).
- Increased KV cache TTLs for high-frequency prefixes to reduce eviction churn (rolled patch at 13:12 PST).
- Bypassed the problematic autoscaler heuristic for the affected pool (manual override ongoing).

Next steps (owner):
- Collect full system traces and the kernel-level OOM/paging logs (Sergio).
- Reproduce offline with a traffic replay and confirm whether a quantization-induced mem pattern triggers the page faults (Hannah).
- Draft customer-facing RCA and timeline (Jasmine).

Attachments: system-trace-logs-20271101.zip (server traces + heap snapshots)

Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@fluxdata.com>, FluxData SRE <sre@fluxdata.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Draft RCA and remediation plan — FluxData us-west-2 throughput incident (Nov 1)

Hi Alex / Priya — attaching a short RCA draft and remediation plan for the Nov 1st inference degradation. Key items below, full doc attached (20271103-fluxdata-rca-draft.pdf) and we've shared a working copy on Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/FluxData-RCA-2027-11-03

Executive summary:
- Impact: 12:44–13:12 PST on 2027-11-01. Throughput reduced by ~40% for FluxData steady-state load; some client retries observed.
- Root cause: A sudden request-pattern change created pathological KV cache churn on the serving pool, which combined with an autoscaler delay and a kernel-level page-fault pattern on new instances that prolonged cold-starts. The result was reduced batching efficiency and elevated tail latencies.

Timeline (high level):
- 12:44 PST — request pattern changes; KV eviction rate spikes.
- 12:50 PST — autoscaler schedules additional instances.
- 12:56–13:06 PST — new instances experience high page-fault rates during initialization, delaying readiness.
- 13:00 PST — Redwood applies emergency routing to warm replicas.
- 13:12 PST — temporary cache TTL changes and autoscaler heuristic bypassed; throughput returns to baseline by 13:20 PST.

Remediation (proposed and timeline):
1) Short term (1–3 days):
   - Harden autoscaler health checks to avoid false-ready signals (owner: Infra Eng; ETA: 3 days).
   - Increase default KV TTL for high-frequency prefixes and add prefix heat detection (owner: Serving Runtime; ETA: 48 hours).
2) Medium term (2–4 weeks):
   - Add kernel-level guard in VM initialization to pre-touch pages for common model quant configs (owner: Platform; ETA: 2 weeks).
   - Improve batching fallback logic to prevent efficiency collapse when batch size drops below threshold (owner: Runtime; ETA: 3 weeks).
3) Ops & customers:
   - New runbook for traffic spikes and cache churn (owner: CS + SRE; ETA: 5 days).
   - Offer FluxData a follow-up call to review changes and a commitment to monitor the affected pool for 30 days.

Requested confirmation from FluxData:
- Are you comfortable with the proposed short-term mitigations and the 30-day monitoring window?
- Do you want an SLA credit estimate for the impacted window (we can escalate to finance if you prefer)?

Attachments: 20271103-fluxdata-rca-draft.pdf

Thanks — we want to make sure the plan meets your needs and will prioritize the short-term fixes.

Best regards,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fluxdata.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@fluxdata.com>, FluxData SRE <sre@fluxdata.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft RCA and remediation plan — FluxData us-west-2 throughput incident (Nov 1)

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear plan. We reviewed the draft and the timeline looks reasonable. Two quick asks:

1) Please confirm when the short-term changes are live (cache TTL + autoscaler bypass).
2) We would like an SLA credit estimate for the impacted window; please escalate to your billing team and send a proposed credit amount.

Otherwise we're happy to proceed with your plan and schedule a technical review next week to walk through the kernel/page-fault findings.

Appreciate the responsiveness — Alex
Alex Nguyen
SRE, FluxData Labs
